title: Staff Engineer — large payments company
description: A peer company is hiring at staff level on a platform team. The work is recognisably the work you already do, one rung up.

strong.headline: They came back fast and asked to move quickly.

success.headline: Your application got through to a real conversation.

nearMiss.headline: A recruiter replied, mostly to say the bar had moved.

failure.headline: No reply. You learned what that pile looks like from the inside.

title: Senior Engineer — grid modelling startup
description: Twenty people, three years of runway, working on electricity grid forecasting. They would pay you noticeably less than you earn now.

strong.headline: The founder replied personally within a day.

success.headline: They want to talk. They were direct about the pay.

nearMiss.headline: They were interested and then went quiet — a funding round is closing.

failure.headline: They passed. They wanted someone who had already worked in energy.

title: Tech Lead — logistics scale-up
description: Leading a team of six. More of the job is people than code, which is the part you have the least evidence for.

strong.headline: They liked that you had been mentoring, and said so.

success.headline: They want to explore it, with questions about your management experience.

nearMiss.headline: They liked you and could not get past the missing leadership track record.

failure.headline: They wanted someone who had already run a team.

title: Infrastructure Engineer — AI research lab
description: A serious research lab needs someone to build the systems the researchers run on. The applicant pool is enormous and unusually strong.

strong.headline: Someone senior there had read something you wrote.

success.headline: You got past the first filter, which most people do not.

nearMiss.headline: They kept your application on file, which they say to everyone and occasionally mean.

failure.headline: Nothing. The pool was full of people who had done this exact thing before.

title: Engineering Manager — internal move
description: Your own company is opening a manager role one team over. Everyone involved already knows your work, for better and worse.

strong.headline: Your manager put your name forward before you finished asking.

success.headline: You are a candidate. Internally, that is already public.

nearMiss.headline: They want you to do it informally for a while first.

failure.headline: They went external. You are now visibly someone who wanted it.

title: Two months of advisory work, evenings
description: A former colleague's company wants eight hours a week of your time on their data platform. It pays, and it ends.

strong.headline: You fixed something they had lived with for a year. They told people.

success.headline: You did the work and got paid for it.

nearMiss.headline: The engagement fizzled halfway through when their priorities moved.

failure.headline: It ate your evenings and produced very little either of you would point at.

title: Deliver what is already on your plate
description: The roadmap work. Nobody will be surprised by it, and it is the reason you are trusted.

strong.headline: You shipped more than anyone expected in the time.

success.headline: You shipped what you said you would.

nearMiss.headline: It slipped, for the ordinary reasons things slip.

failure.headline: The work stalled on something outside your control.

title: Take the migration nobody wants to own
description: High profile, badly scoped, and watched by people two levels above you. It will go visibly well or visibly badly.

strong.headline: It landed cleanly and the people who noticed were the right ones.

success.headline: It landed. Late, but it landed.

nearMiss.headline: Half of it shipped and the rest is still open.

failure.headline: It went badly in public. You now know exactly why.

title: Take on two of the new engineers
description: Nobody asked you to. It will not show up anywhere formal for a long time.

strong.headline: One of them is visibly better because of you, and says so where it counts.

success.headline: They are getting better, slowly, and they trust you.

nearMiss.headline: You gave a lot of time to someone who left anyway.

failure.headline: It turned into answering the same question repeatedly.

title: Fix the deployment system nobody owns
description: Everyone loses an hour a week to it. Fixing it is real work that will be almost impossible to point at afterwards.

strong.headline: It works now. The team noticed for about a week.

success.headline: It is meaningfully better and almost nobody knows why.

nearMiss.headline: You made it better and something else broke.

failure.headline: You spent the time and it is roughly where it was.

title: Ask for the promotion
description: Put together the case, have the conversation, and find out what your manager actually thinks.

strong.headline: It went through, and faster than the usual cycle.

success.headline: It went through at the next cycle.

nearMiss.headline: Not this cycle. You now have a written list of what would change that.

failure.headline: It was not close, and the conversation was more honest than comfortable.

title: Go properly deep on distributed systems
description: The papers, not the blog posts. You already know most of the shape of this.

strong.headline: Several things you had been treating as folklore turned out to have reasons.

success.headline: You understand a layer further down than you did.

nearMiss.headline: You got through some of it before work took the evenings back.

failure.headline: You read it and very little stuck without something to use it on.

title: Learn machine learning from the bottom
description: Slow, unglamorous, and the entry ticket to a set of roles that are currently closed to you.

strong.headline: It clicked, and faster than you expected it to.

success.headline: You can follow the papers now, mostly.

nearMiss.headline: You got through the maths and ran out of turns before the interesting part.

failure.headline: It was harder going than you wanted to admit.

title: Get better at writing things down
description: Design docs, arguments, explanations. The skill that quietly gates most of the roles above yours.

strong.headline: A document you wrote settled an argument that had been running for months.

success.headline: Your writing is tighter and people are reading further into it.

nearMiss.headline: You practised without anyone reading the result.

failure.headline: You wrote a lot of words nobody needed.

title: Use what you have been learning on something real
description: Take the thing you have been studying and put it into work that other people depend on.

strong.headline: It worked in production and now there is something to point at.

success.headline: You used it for real, which is the part that makes it stick.

nearMiss.headline: You got it working and then the project was reprioritised.

failure.headline: It did not survive contact with the real system.

title: Build the tool you keep wishing existed
description: A weekend's worth of scaffolding, then however much you feed it. Nobody has asked for it.

strong.headline: It works, it is documented, and two strangers have already opened issues.

success.headline: It works. You are the only user so far.

nearMiss.headline: It half works and you know exactly which half.

failure.headline: You lost the thread of it somewhere around the third evening.

title: Write the series you keep drafting in your head
description: Six pieces on the thing you actually know about. It costs project time and pays in reputation.

strong.headline: One of the pieces got passed around by people you have never met.

success.headline: You published them. A few hundred people read the good one.

nearMiss.headline: You published two of six and stopped.

failure.headline: The drafts are still drafts.

title: Build the thing a small charity keeps asking for
description: A caseworker you met needs something that does not exist. It is unglamorous and someone would use it on Monday.

strong.headline: They are using it daily and have asked what else you could build.

success.headline: They are using it. It saves someone about an hour a day.

nearMiss.headline: You built it and the person who wanted it changed jobs.

failure.headline: What they needed turned out not to be what they asked for.

title: Put the project in front of people
description: Stop polishing it. Announce it, post it, send it to the people who might care, and find out.

strong.headline: It found its people. The traffic did not stop after the first day.

success.headline: A real number of people showed up and some of them stayed.

nearMiss.headline: A flurry on the first day and nothing after it.

failure.headline: You launched it and nobody came.

title: Get back in touch with people you have lost track of
description: Six or seven messages to people you used to work with. Not asking for anything.

strong.headline: Two of them wanted to talk properly, and one of them is hiring.

success.headline: Several good conversations, no particular outcome.

nearMiss.headline: Polite replies from people who are very busy.

failure.headline: Mostly silence. It has been a while.

title: Go to the conference this month
description: Three days, most of it useless, and occasionally the entire point of a year.

strong.headline: You met someone whose work you had followed for years, and they remembered yours.

success.headline: A good haul of conversations and two people worth staying in touch with.

nearMiss.headline: You spent most of it standing near conversations rather than in them.

failure.headline: Three days, some talks you could have watched later, nobody new.

title: Have coffee with people doing interesting things
description: Four conversations with people whose work you do not understand yet. No agenda.

strong.headline: One of those conversations is going to change what you do next. You cannot tell which yet.

success.headline: Interesting. Nothing you can act on.

nearMiss.headline: Two cancelled. The others were pleasant.

failure.headline: You spent four hours being told about other people's jobs.

title: Publish something about what you actually know
description: One piece, properly done, on the problem you have spent two years inside.

strong.headline: It travelled further than anything you have written. Recruiters noticed.

success.headline: It was read by the people it was for.

nearMiss.headline: Well received by four people, three of whom you know.

failure.headline: You published it into silence.

title: Give the talk
description: Forty minutes in front of a hundred people who work on similar problems. You would have to write it first.

strong.headline: People queued afterwards. Two of them wanted to talk about jobs.

success.headline: It went well. A handful of people found you afterwards.

nearMiss.headline: The talk was fine and the room was half empty.

failure.headline: You lost the room about ten minutes in and knew it.
